Строка та же, а токены разные. У PaLI-X: The string is the same, but the tokens differ. In PaLI-X, the number 255 is the ordinary token “255”, one of the thousand number tokens in the vocabulary. The PaLM-E vocabulary has no separate tokens for numbers, so the authors overwrote the 256 least frequently used tokens to represent actions: bin 255 is a rare token that used to mean something else and now means “gripper open”. In both cases the action takes eight tokens, and the words of answers stay in the vocabulary next to them.

Web pairs in every batch keep the encoder and the words from drifting apart: the model remembers what purple looks like and goes on describing images. On our small model, the difference in actions between the two methods is small and depends on the seed: over three seeds, the co-fine-tuned model picks up purple in 7–18 scenes, and the one fine-tuned on actions in 9–16; on seed C the co-fine-tuned one even falls behind. What differs consistently is the captions: 47–48 of 48 versus 22–35. In the paper, too, the gap in actions is small at 5B parameters, 44% versus 42%, while at 55B it's 63% versus 52%; the authors explain the gain by the model not forgetting concepts.
